title: Support-Vector Networks (SVMs)
hook: An SVM draws the decision boundary that maximizes the gap to the nearest training points - the wider the margin, the better it generalizes to new data.
key_points: The decision boundary is chosen to maximize the margin: the gap between the two classes' closest points.
Only the training points nearest the boundary - the support vectors - determine it; other points don't matter.
The soft-margin variant allows some misclassifications, controlled by a penalty parameter C.
Combined with kernels, SVMs can learn nonlinear boundaries without explicitly computing high-dim features.
Was the dominant classifier for images and text before deep learning surpassed it.
content_html: A support vector machine finds the line (or hyperplane, in higher dimensions) that separates two classes with the largest possible gap on either side. The intuition is that a wider margin means the classifier is less fragile - small shifts in new data are less likely to push points across the boundary.
extra_html:
How it works

The boundary is defined entirely by the training points closest to it - the support vectors. This gives the algorithm a kind of compression: you can discard all other training points and still reconstruct the exact model. In the real world, classes often overlap, so the soft-margin SVM introduced by Cortes and Vapnik allows some points to be on the wrong side, penalized by a tunable constant. Extending SVMs to nonlinear problems is done with the kernel trick.

Why it matters

The 1995 paper by Cortes and Vapnik introduced a framework with strong theoretical backing in statistical learning theory, and SVMs dominated benchmark results for a decade. Understanding them builds intuition for margin-based thinking and regularization that applies well beyond SVMs themselves. The original paper remains a clear read for the core theory.

flashcards.prompt: What criterion does an SVM use to choose its decision boundary?
flashcards.back_html: It maximizes the margin - the gap between the boundary and the closest points of each class - since a wider margin generalizes better.

choices.text: The training points nearest the boundary, which alone determine it
The points farthest from the boundary
The features with the highest variance

flashcards.explanation_html: Only the closest points define the boundary; you can discard all others and reconstruct the same model.

flashcards.prompt: What does the soft-margin SVM's penalty parameter C control?

choices.text: How much misclassification of overlapping points is tolerated
The number of support vectors allowed
The dimensionality of the kernel feature space

flashcards.explanation_html: Real classes overlap, so the soft-margin variant allows some wrong-side points, penalized by the tunable constant C.
